one_liner: systeme.io has a documented REST public API that uses a self-generated X-API-Key header, and a free plan that never expires. A third-party review says it also has an official MCP server. No OAuth is documented.
auth_notes: The official API docs say an API key in the X-API-Key header is the only option right now. Keys are created in Settings under "MCP & API keys", with an optional expiry date. The draft's "up to 3 keys" claim and its Rollout-guide OAuth note do not appear in the supplied pages, so I dropped both.
access_notes: The free plan is permanent and needs no credit card, and keys are generated self-serve in account settings. The pages never say that API keys are restricted to paid plans. The pricing page lists "API requests per minute" as a plan feature, but its values did not render. So the rate limit may vary by plan, but I can't confirm that.
blocker_notes: Each user must paste their own API key, because there is no OAuth. The rate limit is shared across all of a user's keys. The draft's MCP URL (mcp.systeme.io/mcp) is not in the supplied pages, so I set it to null. MCP is rated official on the strength of a third-party review and the vendor's help article, which describes MCP keys in settings. No vendor MCP page was fetched.
